A_target.statement:
Let $G$ be a [[Definition:Finite Graph|finite graph]].
Then the number of [[Definition:Vertex of Graph|vertices]] of $G$ of [[Definition:Odd Integer|odd]] [[Definition:Degree of Vertex|degree]] is [[Definition:Even Integer|even]].

B_source.statement:
Let $G = \struct {V, E}$ be a [[Definition:Finite Graph|finite graph]].
Then:
:$\displaystyle \sum_{v \mathop \in V} \map \deg v = 2 \card E$

substitutions.the full degree sum sum_v deg(v): split into even-degree and odd-degree contributions
substitutions.2|E| (even): the parity constraint on the total

derived.sum of odd degrees must be even: there are an even number of odd terms

validity_conditions: By handshaking, sum_v deg(v) = 2|E| is even.
Split the sum into even-degree vertices (contributing an even total) and odd-degree vertices.
For the overall sum to be even, the number of odd terms must be even - so the count of odd-degree vertices is even.
proof_plan:
From the [[Handshake Lemma]]:
:$\displaystyle \sum_{v \mathop \in V} \map \deg v = 2 \card E$
which is [[Definition:Even Integer|even]].

Let $V_0$ and $V_1$ be the sets of vertices of even and odd degree respectively.
Then:
:$\displaystyle \sum_{v \mathop \in V_0} \map \deg v + \sum_{v \mathop \in V_1} \map \deg v = 2 \card E$
The first sum is [[Definition:Even Integer|even]], so $\displaystyle \sum_{v \mathop \in V_1} \map \deg v$ is even.
